text:
oliver: Quick benchmarks summary (streaming SSE vs non-streaming WS) across GPUs/regions. Ran steady-state and ramp tests for seq<=512, models: small-mid instruction models (7B-ish). Main findings: streaming lowers tail latency but can reduce peak throughput under high concurrent connections. Details + links below.

oliver: TL;DR:
- p50: SSE ~20–60ms lower than WS for single-request patterns (depends on kernel/hw).
- p95: SSE wins 20–120ms (best on a100-80 when fused kernels enabled).
- throughput (req/s): WS with batching > SSE at high concurrency (WS batching scales better on same node).
- quantization (8-bit FP) increased throughput ~25% but caused small quality regressions on instruction-following evals (ROUGE -2.0 to -3.5).
- kernel note: fused-attn + cublas-fft picks improved streaming latency for seq<=512; for seq>1024 the benefit drops.

oliver: Charts/dashboards (internal): https://redwood.internal/bench/streams-vs-ws-1763508272
Raw CSV: https://redwood.internal/storage/bench/1763508272/results.csv

oliver: Repro command we used (CI harness):
```bash
rbench run \\--model rwd-instr-7b \\--gpu a100-80 \\--region us-east1 \\--mode streaming \\--concurrency 1,8,32,128 \\--seq 512 \\--quant none
```

anya: Nice summary. Two quick Qs: did you run with CPU offload on for the a100 runs? and what kernel flags did you set (fused-attn on/off)?

oliver: CPU offload: disabled for a100-80 and a100-40 baseline runs, enabled only in a subset of low-memory T4 tests. Kernel flags: fused-attn=on, flash-attn toggled per-run; we kept heuristic kernel selection enabled for the main sweep and forced specific kernels in an A/B subtest.

raj: For capacity planning: from the throughput CSV, approximate numbers I extracted -> for rwd-instr-7b seq512:
- SSE (streaming): peak ~650 req/s per a100-80 node at concurrency mix we tested
- WS (batching): peak ~1200 req/s per a100-80 node with batch size 8
So for a 1k sustained qps service (mixed requests) you'd need ~2 nodes (WS) vs ~2 (SSE) for pure throughput, but SSE needs more headroom to maintain tail latency under spikes. In practice I'd plan 3-4 nodes for SSE to keep p95 under SLA.

ci-bot: Automated run summary: 1763508272-run1 -> a100-80 us-east1: streaming p50=92ms p95=212ms throughput=640 rps; non-streaming p50=168ms p95=330ms throughput=1180 rps; 8-bit quant streaming p95 degraded by +30ms and eval score -2.7.

lina: On the eval side: the instruction-following evals (prompt set IF-120) showed more hallucinations post-quant for a small subset of prompts. We should add a regression alert to Optimize that triggers on eval delta >1.5 points for production canaries.

anya: Curious about region differences — anything surprising between us-east and eu-west?

oliver: eu-west (a100-40) behaved similarly for latency percentiles but peak throughput dropped ~15% vs a100-80. ap-south (t4) latency p95 was much higher and batching couldn't recover throughput due to memory limits. So region routing policy should prefer a100 pools for latency-sensitive streaming endpoints.

raj: Kernel-wise, if fused-attn gives latency wins on SSE, can we force it only for SSE routes? Any downside?

oliver: We can. Downside: fused kernels sometimes increase memory pressure and make quantization/memory-offload combos unstable. We'll add a preflight test for fused+quant combos.

lina: Proposed next steps:
- add an Optimize alert for quant quality regressions (IF-120 delta)
- canary SSE for latency-sensitive routes in us-east1 with auto-fallback to WS when concurrency > threshold
- run fused-attn + 8-bit preflight matrix across seq 128/512/1024 and capture mem OOM rates

oliver: Sounds good. I'll open a short RFC and add the CSV/plots into the RFC doc. Can folks reply with any missing test permutations (e.g., different batch sizes or model variants)?

anya: Add CPU-offload=true runs for the a100-40 tests, and force flash-attn off for a couple runs to compare.

raj: I'll add capacity calc rows for 250/500/1000/2000 qps for us-east/eu-west and share by EOD.

ci-bot: Created issue #RM-1423: "SSE vs WS benchmark follow-ups" (link: https://redwood.internal/issues/RM-1423).

oliver: Thanks all. Leaving the CSV and a one-page summary in the RFC. :thumbsup:
